description:
Pre-public-release cleanup: `git log --all --format='%an <%ae>' | sort -u` shows two authors:
- mudbungie <mudbungie@gmail.com>  (correct)
- Tester <t@t.local>                (placeholder, leaked from agent runs without git config)

Once the repo is public, every visitor sees these in `git log`. Rewrite history to remap Tester→mudbungie before the first public push.

Approach:
- Use `git filter-repo --email-callback` (preferred; install if missing) or `git filter-branch --env-filter` as fallback
- Map: GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL/GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL t@t.local → mudbungie@gmail.com; GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_NAME Tester → mudbungie
- Apply to all refs (main, balls/tasks, archive/*, etc. — `git for-each-ref` to enumerate first)
- Verify post-rewrite: `git log --all --format='%an <%ae>' | sort -u` shows only mudbungie

Caveats — this task does NOT fit the standard worktree-and-merge flow cleanly:
- The rewrite operates on the canonical .git, not just the worktree's branch tip
- After the rewrite, working trees and main both reset to new SHAs; there is no file diff to squash on `bl review`
- Plan: claim normally to get a worktree; perform the rewrite; if `bl review` rejects (nothing to squash), drop the claim and `bl update status=closed --note '...'` to archive the ball with a record

Gates:
- tests: rebuild and verify `cargo test --no-run` still compiles after rewrite (refs changed, content unchanged — should be fine)
- docs: N/A (no doc impact)
- alignment: aligns with the going-public goal

WARNING: history rewrite is destructive. Confirm with the user before pushing if any remote tracking has been set up. Currently the repo has no public remote, so the rewrite is local-only and reversible (the original refs land in .git/refs/original/ from filter-branch, or in a backup ref from filter-repo).
title: Rewrite git history: remap Tester <t@t.local> author to mudbungie <mudbungie@gmail.com>
